title: Provenance labels and the limits of detection

sources.claim: Content provenance (for example C2PA Content Credentials) records signed information about how a file was made or edited; the record can be stripped by re-uploading or screenshots, a missing record does not show that content is real or fake, and watermark detection is probabilistic, with false positives and false negatives.

sections.skill: Explain provenance labels and the limits of detection

questions.domain: Creative: audio, music, video and synthetic media
questions.prompt: What does provenance mean?

choices.text: A record of where content came from and how it changed
A rating of how beautiful or well made a picture is compared with other pictures online

questions.correct_answer: A record of where content came from and how it changed
questions.intro: PROVENANCE means a record of where content came from and how it was changed. CONTENT CREDENTIALS, based on the C2PA standard (Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity), attach signed information to a file, such as which camera or tool made it and what edits were applied. WATERMARKS are hidden or visible marks some generators add to their output. These help, but they have LIMITS. Records can be stripped by screenshots or re-uploading. A MISSING label does not prove content is real or fake. DETECTOR tools give scores, often shown as percentages, and make errors both ways.

sections.skill: Compare provenance with a package tracking history

questions.domain: Creative: audio, music, video and synthetic media
questions.prompt: What does a tracking history show?
questions.intro: A package TRACKING HISTORY shows where a parcel has been: shipped from the warehouse, scanned in your city, delivered. It helps you trust the package came from the right place. But if someone repacks the item in a plain box, the history is gone, and a box with no tracking is not necessarily stolen. Provenance records work similarly: helpful when present, easy to lose, and their absence proves little.

sections.title: Apply it

questions.domain: Creative: audio, music, video and synthetic media
questions.prompt: A detector answers YES when it judges an image AI-made. What is a false positive?

choices.text: Flagging a real photo as AI

questions.correct_answer: Flagging a real photo as AI
questions.intro: Detector scores are especially easy to misuse. A detector that says "85% likely AI" is not proof; it can wrongly flag real photos (FALSE POSITIVES) and miss fakes (FALSE NEGATIVES). Using a score alone to accuse someone, such as a student of cheating or a journalist of faking, can cause real harm. Treat provenance and detection as one clue among several, alongside source, context and confirmation.
